evidenceDecision: React 19 (#679): the installed client and profiling development renderers are mounted in isolated DOM runtimes; changed object-array getter counts enforce bounded diagnostic traversal while retaining changed-prop entries and actual UI updates. Direct Chrome Board comparisons with CPU profiling on/off establish the observed stall and its removal (docs/react-19.md). This is dependency instrumentation and browser evidence, not a new authority/recovery contract or a model of React scheduling. Group CLI: direct service/parser/transport tests cover crew-governed edits, actual sender attribution, explicit pooled-role transfers and complete promotion mappings; actual native move fixtures plus the service adapter cover one shared queue, generation retirement, complete printed-effect revalidation, terminal witnesses and failed partial Board reconciliation. Sources freshness tests distinguish current counts from stale/unavailable work. These finite transforms and controlled promise schedules exercise the actual adapters rather than restating them in a model. Actual production-context/browser/layout and generated site-content tests exercise rendering, search projection and published content. Board (PR #215): placement, the gesture state machine, the board store, anchors and move-following are checked directly. Pure-function unit tests cover every anchor state, empty and partial witnesses, desk, pane and rolled-back move outcomes, conditional detach and kept-draft storage across tabs. Service tests cover Send revalidation against the saved board and start identity. Browser races at 1440 and 390 px cover late absence replies, two-client layout and draft conflicts. A model would restate these small pure rules, while real Herdr restart and ID reuse behaviour was verified only in throwaway sessions. Relations (FM-TEAMS): which terminals know each other is a pure function of the saved document and the current observations; unit tests cover each evidence source and its system of record, token supersession, pane moves (terminal identity), cross-connection refusal (in the shared rules the service applies), stale evidence kept as stale while a host is offline, pruning only from a complete current snapshot, one claim per child and generation-qualified recording that reads only live snapshots (relying on Q10's stale/non-actionable cached topology). Group join/leave rules, colour inheritance (a chosen colour always wins) and the stamp command are tested directly; Town and Board browser tests at 1440 and 390 px drag desks and cards together, group and ungroup. The spawn token's shape, and that a Herdr restart reuses pane IDs but issues new terminal IDs (so pre-restart evidence is never matched by pane ID, and is dropped once a complete snapshot shows its terminals closed), were confirmed against Herdr 0.9.3 in throwaway sessions. Stored Groups: direct exhaustive tests enumerate 36 two-pod role combinations for pooled lead/builder exclusivity and shared reviewers; service regressions cover atomic confirmed transfers on join/set_roles/promote, legacy read-only migration, Team-only pruning and magnetic consumers, canonical address resolution across restart/away/ambiguity, per-connection/member/role caps, stale revisions, full 64-entry promotion diffs and the 128-event retention/deletion boundary. This is bounded pure state validation plus existing Board atomic persistence, not a new ordering or authenticated-principal protocol; a separate model would duplicate these finite rules. Browser consumers retain their actual Board/Town grouping and undo checks. Sender attribution does not enforce the owner/FirstMate crew rule. Reviewer RESULT evidence (#369): direct parser/decoder/static-render/readiness fixtures cover explicit sender claims (not verified identities), stable separately linked unknown sources, shared-login refusal, quoted author replies, formal metadata or unique explicit SHA binding, ambiguity/conflicts/stale heads, typed open findings and unknown-over-clear refusal with open-first precedence. The browser-only PR action tests remain mandatory. This bounded text/data projection does not add an authority or scheduling model; real GitHub completeness and browser interaction remain platform/consumer evidence. Harness readiness: complete-record/status fixtures distinguish confirmed missing/sign-out from unknown transport, timeout, malformed and unsupported probes; shared wire/parser and static markup preserve safe provenance/freshness and retry/configuration presentation. RPC tests bind discovery/process observations to the captured host and reject retirement through the existing generation-qualified reply publisher. Native CLI/SSH/auth and viewport interaction remain platform/browser acceptance. Failed-host recovery: exact-owner/generation lifecycle metadata immediately retires cached actions through pending snapshots; deferred Board rendering cannot retain a live retired target, cached agent activity stays unknown/static, and explicit recovery uses one captured profile. Controlled scheduler tests cover more than six transient failures then recovery, finite policy and cancellation/removal with a healthy sibling. No real-network liveness or viewport claim follows from these fixtures. PR detail freshness: controlled-clock/deferred-query fixtures distinguish list success from complete head/stamp-qualified detail, retain stale evidence with original read time, preserve 10/20 bounds/fair ordering, isolate configuration cache writers and refuse expiry/retirement during live native merge admission. Shared/browser consumers reject missing or malformed freshness and retain qualified links. No GitHub history completeness, network liveness or rollback after dispatch is claimed. Owner ask presentation (#472) uses direct qualified-target, bounded queue and mark-priority cases plus the actual Town, Board and Desk browser suites. The real ledger's occupant-scoped keyed withdrawal never creates a question. Pure projection and the Town browser test place a shell question before at least six finishes and open its original terminal once. Owner asks (#493): service tests place an unverified pane claim only when exactly one local Herdr has the pane (never a remote, unknown or ambiguous one), keep it unverified for keys and allowance, record Herdr's agent name, and close a dismissed ask for waits, answers and keyed repeats until the asker withdraws. Placement finishes before the synchronous cause, allowance and insertion step, and a slow-Herdr case checks concurrent keyed repeats and the shared unverified allowance. Every ask from one pane resolves to that pane, and Open agent opens a shell asker's terminal. Pure naming, rail markup and the Town browser case cover an unverified placed ask at reception, one unverified mark, Open agent and Dismiss without an answer. No new transport or authenticated-principal model is claimed. Cold-entry regressions initialize browser storage and load the asks model before the application store in a fresh process. The real main.tsx is served by Vite to Chrome with owned synthetic proxy traffic; startup errors and ErrorBoundary output fail the check before mounted-shell acceptance. Late notifier installation preserves backlog suppression and one new-ask announcement. This covers the shipped entry and reported module order, not arbitrary JavaScript dependency graphs. Board follow-ups (#222): native-order qualified attention and appearance validation use direct fixtures; the real Board browser covers status/surface persistence and mouse/touch single-pane moves with cancellation and last-room confirmation. The historical owner maximum (3 hosts, 8 workspaces each, 15 tabs each) runs Board and Town through the same native-input/CDP harness and work ceilings. These are consumer/browser measurements; no new unbounded ordering or latency claim is made. Group projections use direct pure-function evidence: all 36 six-state roll-up pairs, qualified Room/Desk membership, canonical identity admission through both service and browser adapters, away/ambiguity exclusion, deduplicated work and current runtime/session link matching. These observational transformations introduce no new scheduling or action authority; actual UI and gesture evidence remains independently required. The Town reflow hold (wait while pressed and for the quiet period after, explicit Fold/Expand bypass, a later background change waiting again, dropping a held layout that names a removed desk, a new shape placing at once) is checked headless in the scene model on a manual clock, each case failing on its mutant; the browser keeps one wiring case in the extended suite, where a real canvas press holds a background reflow until release. Town camera rules (home on wide and phone, zoom steps out to in including the phone whole-town step, Show the whole town, keyboard pans, focus near edges or at town level, a room request run once per seq without replay after its room leaves and returns, re-framing only while at home, the reflow follow and the pose kept per shape) are checked headless on the scene camera, each failing on its mutant; the browser keeps the delayed-renderer room request, the room card zoom and slow-frame zoom cases. Town pointer interaction (taps, room and building zooms, touch holds, mouse lifts, moves, reorders, groups after the magnet time, the magnet restarting whenever the town moves under a still carry (edge pan, camera moves, a renderer drawing slower than the pan) and never starting, or firing, while the carry is in the edge band or a zoom, flight or fling is still to be drawn, even with frames further apart than its wait; disposing cancels a pending magnet, a carry looking through agents walking, queued or lounging over a floor or desk (neither their room, their desk nor the magnet), such an agent picked up where it walks while its empty chair is its pane, ungroups, agent moves, uncertain outcomes, drops outside a building, edge pan per frame, re-aim after a drawn pan, presses against the last drawn camera, wheel and trackpad zoom, double taps, hover and pinch) is checked headless with test frames and a manual clock, each rule failing on its mutant; the browser keeps the real DOM pointer path, edge scroll under slow frames and drop evidence. What the Town renderer bakes again after a change is checked headless: unchanged inputs and agent status bake nothing; a desk colour, pin, room carpet, host colour, host theme, host staleness, seat count or room rectangle bakes only its building; a seeded 160-step walk paints every building with the renderer's own painters on recording canvases and requires baking only dirty buildings to match a full repaint; the town size or a building rectangle rebuilds the scene; over every pair of seven variants, dirty sets bake exactly when the previous whole-world key rebuilt, and a seeded 200-step walk keeps a recording renderer equal to a full bake. The Town browser case requires a room and a building colour to bake their building again without a scene rebuild. Which Town agents the renderer reconciles is checked headless: an unchanged observation reconciles none and builds no navigation; one status, summoned or asking change reconciles only its host; over seeded 300-step walks (with and without reduced motion) a TownActors reconciling only dirty hosts stays equal, field by field, to one reconciling every host after each observation and after walking; the Town browser case requires an unchanged observation to reconcile no agent and one status change to reconcile fewer than all agents without building navigation. Town's HUD topics are checked headless on a manual clock: what is on screen and the zoom level publish only when they change (idle frames and small pans publish nothing), frame followers hear each drawn frame, waiting ages move on every 15 s only while shown and stop with the last viewer, and connector anchors (seat, standing, desk; clamped 10 px inside with the edge named) are computed from world geometry. Things that follow drawn frames move in place without React commits, checked under happy-dom with the React Profiler (frameFollowers.dom.test.ts): a walking agent's Inspector connector moves through the anchor feed and World commits only when an anchor appears or goes, and a desk badge popover follows a panning camera with zero commits; each fails on its mutant. Shared Town move orchestration is checked through the actual RPC adapter and native move functions with controlled promise schedules: shared service queue identity, stale queued generation, known partial reconciliation, unknown topology without retry or anchor guessing, and appearance/Board reconciliation before the next queued move starts. These are bounded adapter/recovery cases under the existing move contract, not a new queue algorithm or temporal progress claim. Shared terminal appearance uses the actual RPC handler in a 64-case connection/generation/witness/read-retirement matrix, persistent document/migration/move tests, a held old acknowledgement consumer, and two isolated desktop/phone Chrome profiles driving the real editor against the real handler/store with synthetic native replies/events. Bounds and missing atomic native rename preconditions are explicit in verification/contracts/shared-appearance.md; existing lifecycle, Bridge and platform consumers remain mandatory. Existing CLI colour/Undo consumers also bind current terminal evidence and compare occupant-qualified probes, refusing uncertain legacy undo after migration. Roamgate web sync through 2b16e991 (PR3): All servers reads a fake aggregate observation, keeps overlapping server IDs apart, hides failed, disconnected and replaced runtimes and refuses navigation to them. Tab chips, Pane Search targets, speech text and playback, PDF.js lazy loading (with check-web-assets' production-manifest gate) and opt-in latency samples have direct consumers. No phone smoothness, real speech engine or PDF-viewer detection on every browser is claimed.
